title: Is This Graph a Tree?

concept.title: A tree is a graph that is connected and has exactly n - 1 edges
body: A **tree** is a connected graph without cycles. It has a very handy description in numbers: a graph with `n` nodes is a tree exactly when it is **connected** and has **exactly `n - 1` edges**. (A connected graph needs at least `n - 1` edges to hold together; with exactly that many there is no edge to spare, so no cycle can exist.)

So the test has two parts. First, `m == n - 1` is a one-line check. Second, connectivity: a search from node 1 must reach all `n` nodes. If the edge count is right but the graph is not connected (a triangle and a separate node, for example), then there must be a cycle somewhere, and the graph is not a tree.

body.code:
is_tree = (m == n - 1)
if is_tree:
    # a breadth-first search from node 1 ...
    is_tree = (number of nodes reached == n)

body: Checking the edge count first saves the search when the answer is already "no". The search needs O(n + m) time, and the two conditions together are all one has to know.

statement: An undirected graph has `n` nodes and `m` edges. Print `yes` if the graph is a tree (connected and without cycles) and `no` otherwise.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `m`: the number of nodes (numbered 1 to n) and the number of edges.
Each of the next `m` lines has two numbers `u` and `v`: an edge between the nodes `u` and `v`.
constraints: There are no self-loops and no repeated edges.

examples.note: A path of four nodes: a tree, yes.
Three edges, but they form a triangle and node 4 is alone: no.

hints: A tree with n nodes has exactly n - 1 edges, so compare m with n - 1 first.
Then run a search from node 1 and count the nodes it reaches.
It is a tree only if the count is n.

explanation: A tree has exactly n - 1 edges and is connected. The edge count is compared first; then a search from node 1 must reach all n nodes.
solution.complexity: Time O(n + m), space O(n + m).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m = map(int, input().split())
edges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

adj = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
for u, v in edges:
    adj[u].append(v)
    adj[v].append(u)
ok = (m == n - 1)
if ok:
    seen = [False] * (n + 1)
    seen[1] = True
    queue = [1]
    for v in queue:
        for w in adj[v]:
            if not seen[w]:
                seen[w] = True
                queue.append(w)
    ok = (len(queue) == n)
print("yes" if ok else "no")
